chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hajjaj, from Abdillah ibn al-Walid al-Kindi, from Isma'il ibn Jabir or Abdillah ibn Sinan, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I stand [for night prayer] in the last part of the night and I fear the dawn [will arrive].' He said: 'Recite Al-Hamd [Surah Al-Fatiha] and hurry, hurry.'

This report is applicable to one who is confident that he can complete the night prayer before the dawn rises. As for one who fears [missing it], it is preferable that he offers the Witr [prayer] first, then makes up the eight rak'ahs afterwards. Evidence for this is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: How should one perform night prayer if they are short on time before dawn?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* addresses the practical jurisprudence of Salat al-Layl under time constraints, distinguishing between those confident of completion and those fearing dawn. The Imam’s directive to 'hurry' by reciting only Al-Fatiha highlights the principle of *ikhtisar* (abbreviation) to preserve the prayer's validity, while the commentary advises prioritizing Witr to ensure the essential concluding prayer is not missed. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing spiritual devotion with the legal necessity of fulfilling obligations before the time expires.
